title: Hollow and Choir
premise: Xanthe Thornbury has spent two decades hiding her magic in the city of Vellamere, where a single spark of witchcraft means the gallows. When her date, a gentle lamplighter named Oren, turns out to be named in the Hollow Choir—a book of prophecies written a century before his birth—she learns he is the thirteenth soul sold to the court beneath the mountain, and that the prophecy names her as the thief who must steal it back. Hunted by the city's witch-finders and guided by the ghost of her dead mentor, Xanthe gathers an unlikely found family of outlaws and charmsellers to breach the court. In the end she trades her own hidden memories of her mentor for Oren's soul, discovering that inheritance is not what we keep but what we choose to carry forward.
about_author: Ines Almeida is a former archivist who spent years cataloguing grimoires in a Portuguese monastery before turning to fiction. She writes about magic as inheritance—the things our teachers leave us, whether or not we asked for them.

chapters.title: The Lamplighter's Name
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. On a rare date with Oren, a kind lamplighter, Xanthe glimpses his name glowing in a forbidden prophecy book at a night market—written a century ago, describing tonight exactly. The emotional beat: wonder curdling into dread as her carefully invisible life cracks open.

chapters.title: What the Hedge-Witch Left
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. She returns to her burned-out childhood cottage and summons the ghost of Maren, her executed mentor, who reveals Oren is the thirteenth soul sold to the court beneath the mountain—and that the prophecy names Xanthe as its thief. Emotional beat: grief and guilt resurfacing after twenty years of denial.

chapters.title: Charms for the Gallows-Bound
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. The witch-finders raid the night market; Xanthe escapes with help from Sable, a smuggler who deals in outlawed charms, and Pip, a runaway apprentice like her younger self. Emotional beat: reluctant trust—the first stitches of a found family forming under threat.

chapters.title: Thirteen Turns
chapters.summary: POV: alternating Xanthe and Oren. Oren confesses he has always felt hollow, dreaming of a silver court; the moon's thirteenth turn approaches, when his soul will be fully claimed. Emotional beat: tenderness deepening into resolve—they will not let the prophecy simply happen to them.

chapters.title: The Road Under the Roots
chapters.summary: POV: Sable. The company descends through an old smugglers' road beneath the mountains, navigating Maren's cryptic riddles while witch-finders track them from above. Emotional beat: Sable's cynicism tested as she realizes she cares whether these people live.

chapters.title: The Court Beneath
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. They reach the silver court, where souls are kept as singing instruments in a choir of the sold. Xanthe finds Oren's soul—a small flame humming a lullaby Maren once taught her. Emotional beat: recognition and horror; her past and present are the same song.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Silver
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. The court's sovereign offers a trade: a memory of equal weight for the soul. Xanthe begins surrendering her memories of Maren one by one, feeling herself hollowing even as the flame brightens. Emotional beat: sacrifice as love made tangible.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Thirteenth Turn
chapters.summary: POV: Pip. A member of the company, revealed as a witch-finder informant, triggers a trap as the moon completes its turn; the court moves to claim Oren entirely. Pip chooses courage over survival, buying seconds with a charm that should have killed him. Emotional beat: found family proven in blood.

chapters.title: Hollow and Choir
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Climax. Nearly emptied of memory, Xanthe sings the choir's own song back at the court, waking the stolen souls—including Maren's voice within hers—to shatter the sovereign's claim. She carries Oren's flame out as the mountain's halls collapse into silence. Emotional beat: triumph bought with self-erasure.

chapters.title: What We Choose to Carry
chapters.summary: POV: Xanthe. Above ground, Oren wakes whole though Xanthe cannot remember her teacher's face—but Maren's craft lives in her hands regardless. The city's magic ban begins to crack as witnesses speak. Emotional beat: quiet resolution; inheritance redefined as chosen, not given, and family as the ones who sing you back.
